dispositions.decision: No removal or cut applied. File candidates come from an intentionally narrow source scope with external/classic/ESM host consumers; source inspection has already confirmed the classic HTML loader. Duplicate source variants retain distinct public/loading and host-runtime contracts.

No supported portable hotspot of material size found in this exercised workload. Fetch is asynchronous browser I/O; class methods and closure-owned lifecycle are not eligible pure top-level units. Preserve native Web API behavior, request ownership and cancellation semantics.

Analyzer/profiler suggestions remain candidates, not proven ports. The suggested exported fetch wrapper carries browser-native Headers, Response/ReadableStream, URL, AbortSignal and Promise identities; plain-data bridge assumptions are not met. I/O lifecycle/ownership fixes remove measured duplicate requests directly. No bridge installation, rewrite, activation or unsupported performance claim.

post_challenge_verification.finding: Mutating URL, Headers or RequestInit before the deferred fetch changed the actual request behind an unchanged key.
post_challenge_verification.repair: Transport now consumes the exact copied key inputs. Native Request objects, signals, complex bodies, inherited and non-enumerable dictionary fields retain their intended semantics.
post_challenge_verification.scope_note: Equivalent-work benchmark still measures expired-owner overlap. It is not an app-wide latency or CPU claim.
